correct.evidence: Every date I worked by hand matches: 2026-11-30, 2026-07-03, 2026-06-22, 2020-06-19, 2026-12-23, 2028-01-03, the month clamps, the cap to 2026-05-01, the lead-days 2026-04-28 and 2026-10-06. But on the packaged desktop, POST /v1/schedule is a 500 for every body (finding 1), so SPEC-W2 point 47's desktop serving fails.

sourced.evidence: Holidays are read from the pack's calendar.federal_holidays_law row in force on each day, Juneteenth from its quote, with no number written in engine/schedule.py. All 15 draft quotes are found in the saved copies matched by snapshot_sha256.

never_assumes.evidence: A missing base, cap or setting gives date null with its reason. A day with no holiday row gives 422, not a guess. A base taken from a planning item is not marked planning (finding 8), and a litigated base's status is not on the answer.

inside_the_boundary.evidence: The three drafts and the NO_CALENDAR words are information only. Nothing is addressed to the student or says what anyone should do.

secure.evidence: Both apps refuse the four token forms with 403. But a valid body crashes the packaged route (finding 1), days 1e9, months 1e6 or 0001-01-01 minus 1 day give a 500 OverflowError (finding 6), and an update outside update.schema.json is served (finding 2).

tested.evidence: Mutants M1 (Juneteenth before 2021), M2 (cap + 1 day), M3 (publish_blockers filter removed) and M7 (a day with no holiday row counted) survive. No test runs the routes from the bundled tree, which is why finding 1 was missed.

findings.title: POST /v1/schedule is a 500 on the packaged desktop engine
findings.input: create_app(token) from a tree built from desktop/python/bundle.json alone; POST /v1/schedule with the token and {case: tests' CASE, requests: [{id: a, from: {today: true}, add: {days: 1}, sign: 1}]}
findings.what_happens: 500, FileNotFoundError on contracts/schedule.schema.json, which the bundle does not hold and test_bundle_inputs.py forbids. The repository tree gives 200 with 2026-10-04, so the server and the desktop differ.

findings.title: An update that update.schema.json refuses is served
findings.input: a published file with approval.approved "false", quote_found "false" and checks "no"
findings.what_happens: publish_blockers tests truthiness and returns nothing, so GET /v1/updates serves it. update.schema.json says 'false' is not of type 'boolean'.

findings.title: No test fails when published_updates skips publish_blockers
findings.input: mutant M3: published_updates returns every file
findings.what_happens: Every test passes, because pipeline/published/ does not exist and each test compares an empty list with an empty list.

findings.title: No test pins the cap's boundary day
findings.input: mutant M2 (found > cap_date + 1 day); from 2026-04-30, + 2 days, cap opt.file_by.closes.a1
findings.what_happens: The mutant answers 2026-05-02, past the 2026-05-01 obligation, with no capped flag, and the property test passed.

findings.title: Juneteenth before 2021-06-17 and days with no holiday row are untested
findings.input: mutant M1 (Juneteenth always listed): 2020-06-18 + 1 business day; mutant M7 (no row counts as a business day): 1985-12-30 + 3 business days
findings.what_happens: Both mutants survive. M1 would give 2020-06-22. M7 dates a count that correct code refuses with 422.

findings.title: A body inside the contract overflows to a 500, and a long business-day count stalls
findings.input: {days: 1000000000} from today; {months: 1000000}; {date: 0001-01-01} - 1 day; 1000 requests of about 2,000,000 business days
findings.what_happens: 500 OverflowError in place of 422. Business days run about 5 microseconds each, so the 1000-request body takes hours.

findings.title: The desktop cannot serve a published update
findings.what_happens: pipeline/ is not bundled (test_bundle_inputs forbids it), so the desktop returns an empty list while the server serves the file. api/case.py:85 imports pipeline.graph, which loads langgraph, a package forbidden in the desktop group.

findings.title: A date counted from a planning item is not marked planning
findings.what_happens: Answer 2026-01-14 with no planning flag, although the base item is planning: true. The contract wording allows this; SPEC-W2 point 41 says only when a setting set it.

findings.title: Duplicate ids are accepted; one uncountable request refuses the whole body
findings.input: two requests with id dup; or one 1985 business-day request among others
findings.what_happens: Both dup answers are returned. The 1985 request turns the whole body into a 422.

findings.title: The NAMES pattern differs from openapi's categories pattern
findings.what_happens: Accepted, where openapi's item pattern ^[a-z0-9]+$ would refuse it.
